title: Orchestrated onramp app templates: Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, CLI + retries/streaming cookbook
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Deliver a set of opinionated, production-ready starter templates and cookbook snippets that demonstrate best practices for using Redwood SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go) across common application topologies: Next.js (Edge + Server), FastAPI, Go HTTP server, and a cross-platform CLI. Focus areas: ergonomic streaming consumption (resumable streams, backpressure), robust retry strategies (idempotency keys, exponential backoff, jitter, circuit-breakers), and minimal-boilerplate examples that show token-efficient usage patterns (batching, caching hints, structured outputs). Aim for reproducible examples that teams can fork and run locally or deploy to Vercel/GCP/AWS with a one-command demo script.
acceptance_criteria: Four runnable templates (Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP, CLI) with README and one-click local demo
Patterned retry helpers in Python/TS/Go that handle transient errors and server-side 429/503 semantics
Streaming consumer examples showing resumable reads, incremental rendering (Next.js), and graceful cancellation
Cookbook snippets for common optimizations: batching, KV cache hints, token budgeting, structured output parsing
Automated tests covering retry logic + streaming cancellation behavior (unit + integration), and CI demo deploy workflow
tasks: Design templates scaffold and common SDK helper API surface (retry decorator, stream iterator, context cancellation)
Implement Next.js example with server and edge route demonstrating streaming SSR and client-side SSE fallback
Implement FastAPI example showcasing background streaming tasks, health checks, and retry middleware
Implement idiomatic Go HTTP server example using context cancellation, efficient JSON streaming, and a small KV-cache hint wrapper
Create cross-platform CLI (Python + Go binary + TS Node) examples showing resumable uploads and streaming outputs
Write cookbook.md with concrete snippets: debounced batching, prefix cache TTL best-practices, function calling patterns, structured output schema validation
Add unit/integration tests and CI config for demo deploys (Vercel for Next.js, GitHub Actions for others)
Collect telemetry hooks and sample dashboards links for Console demo (latency/token breakdown)
progress_notes: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting with DX and Product. Agreed scope includes one minimal example per runtime + cookbook snippets. Owner assigned.
2026-03-03: Prototyped TS SSE adapter for Next.js edge; discovered Node fetch streaming differences on Vercel Edge runtime. Decided to provide both edge and server variants in template.
2026-03-05: Python retry decorator v0 implemented (exponential backoff + jitter + idempotency header). Uploaded PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/42

2026-03-07: Go HTTP example benchmarked against small load (100 concurrent clients). Observed context cancel propagation missing in stream handler; hot-fixed handler to stop tokenization goroutine on ctx.Done().

2026-03-09: Design review with PM (Ruth Alvarez) and DX (Maya Park). Feedback: simplify CLI flow, add explicit token budgeting example, and include structured output schema validation for function calling demos.
2026-03-10: Preparing final README drafts and CI workflows. Next steps: tests for retry edge cases and finalize demo deploy scripts.
risks: Edge runtimes have inconsistent streaming semantics (fetch vs. WebSocket) — increased surface area for examples
Users may copy optimistic retry defaults that interact poorly with Dedicated capacity rate limits — need clear guidance in cookbook
Maintaining three language variants for helpers increases maintenance burden; propose extraction of canonical patterns into small single-file helpers per language
test_plan: Unit tests: retry helper behaviors (retry counts, backoff math, idempotency header handling)
Integration tests: simulated 429/503 responses to validate retry + circuit-breaker behavior
Streaming tests: ensure incremental chunks propagate to client and cancellation stops token production
End-to-end smoke: deploy Next.js demo to Vercel preview via GH Action and assert first-byte streaming within latency SLO
demo_steps: ./scripts/setup.sh  # installs deps and sets REDWOOD_API_KEY from .env.example
./scripts/demo-nextjs.sh  # runs local Next.js server with streaming SSR example
./scripts/demo-fastapi.sh  # starts FastAPI server showcasing background streaming and retries
./scripts/demo-go.sh  # builds and runs Go HTTP example; exercise cancellation with curl
./scripts/demo-cli.sh  # Python CLI walkthrough showing resumable streaming and resume token
notes_for_review: Check that retry defaults align with Dedicated capacity rate guidance (PM to approve)
Confirm streaming examples include both SSE and chunked transfer encodings and document differences
Validate that cookbook snippets emphasize idempotency patterns for client-driven retries
